svg.title: Friday — Request flow: replying to an email
svg.text: Friday — Request flow: replying to an email
Two turns. The model drafts the email; the server stops the run before anything is sent, and only his plain yes lets that exact action run.
Turn 1 — he asks; Friday drafts the reply and stops before sending
Turn 2 — he says yes; only that exact action runs
「回一下 John，说我明天下午两点能到」 (Reply to John: I can make it tomorrow at 2)
Instructions for this turn: persona + the time now
call 1: instructions + session history + his message
matching emails, each tagged with its mailbox
tool call: send_email(to, subject, body, mailbox)
needs_approval=True → the run is interrupted; send_email does NOT run
SSE: streamed text · tool events · done {needs_confirm: true}
the card text is written by the server (approval.describe), not by the model
or edits the subject / body in the card → POST /api/chat/revise
Only a plain yes (发 / 好 / 确认 / ok …) approves; 不发 / 取消 / 算了 rejects;
anything else means he moved on, and nothing is sent
send from the mailbox the email came to (Gmail API / SMTP)
closed.record("mail") — a loop closed, counted in the 21:00 wrap-up
What he sees: her bubble with a confirm card
Subject and body can be edited in the card before
sending; the edited version is what he approves.
The recipient cannot be changed there, only by
The paused run lives on disk, so a restart or a
deploy in between does not lose it. If she says
anything else first (a push, the opener), the
Which tools are called, and in what order, is decided by the model at run time; the figure shows the usual path.
If Claude fails mid-turn (no credit, rate limit, outage), src/claude.py asks GPT-5 for the same call and the page folds away the half sentence.
Own to-dos, calendar events and reminders do not stop like this: they run straight away and the reply carries an Undo button (POST /api/undo, no model).
